visṛjya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ śokasaṃvignamānasaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Sañjaya: having spoken thus on the battlefield, Arjuna sat down on the seat of the chariot, casting aside his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed by grief (śoka-saṃvigna-mānasa).
speaker: Sañjaya
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Closing verse of chapter 1: the crisis (grief, śoka) that the teaching of chapter 2 answers.

paraphrase: Chapter 1 sets the scene and the crisis. 1.1: Dhṛtarāṣṭra asks Sañjaya what the two assembled armies did at Kurukṣetra, 'the field of dharma'. 1.2–11: Duryodhana goes to his teacher Droṇa, lists the leading warriors of the Pāṇḍava army (1.4–6) and of his own (1.8–9), compares the two forces (1.10) and orders that Bhīṣma be guarded (1.11). 1.12–19: Bhīṣma and then the Pāṇḍava side (Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna, Bhīma, Yudhiṣṭhira, Nakula, Sahadeva and others) blow their named conches; the uproar rends the Kauravas' hearts. 1.20–27: Arjuna asks Kṛṣṇa to station the chariot between the armies; Kṛṣṇa does so and tells him to look at the assembled Kurus; Arjuna sees his elders, teachers and kin on both sides. 1.28–46: overcome by pity (kṛpā) and despair (viṣāda), Arjuna describes his bodily collapse (1.28–30), says he sees no good (śreyas) in killing kin and wants neither victory nor kingship (1.31–37), argues that destroying a family destroys the family dharmas, leads to varṇa-mixture, the fall of the ancestors and hell (1.38–44), and says it would be better to be killed unresisting (1.45–46). 1.47: Arjuna sits down in the chariot, casting away his bow, his mind overwhelmed by grief (śoka). The chapter's purpose, as it presents itself, is to state Arjuna's grief and his argument from family dharma, which the following teaching answers.
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Printed editions carry a colophon naming the chapter (commonly 'Arjunaviṣādayoga'); the colophon is not among this edition's segments, so it is not quoted here.

original.text:
vedāvināśinaṃ nityaṃ ya enamajamavyayam|
kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṃ ghātayati hanti kam

vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya

original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

original.text:
acchedyo'yamadāhyo'yamakledyo'śoṣya eva ca|
nityaḥ sarvagataḥ sthāṇuracalo'yaṃ sanātanaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

original.text:
avyakto'yamacintyo'yamavikāryo'yamucyate|
tasmādevaṃ viditvainaṃ nānuśocitumarhasi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

tathāpi tvaṃ mahābāho naivaṃ śocitumarhasi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

original.text:
jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyurdhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca|
tasmādaparihārye'rthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
āścaryavatpaśyati kaścidena
māścaryavadvadati tathaiva cānyaḥ|
āścaryavaccainamanyaḥ śrṛṇoti
śrutvāpyenaṃ veda na caiva kaścit
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Cf. Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.2.7 (āścaryo vaktā ...). The last quarter is read either as 'no one at all knows it' or 'some, even having heard, do not know it'; the minimal sense is that hearing alone does not yield knowing. Edition encoding artefact: 'śrṛṇoti' stands for śṛṇoti; the original text is kept exactly as in the segment.

original.text:
dehī nityamavadhyo'yaṃ dehe sarvasya bhārata|
tasmātsarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: this embodied one (dehin) in the body of everyone is forever unslayable (avadhya), Bhārata; therefore you ought not to grieve for any beings.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Closes the first argument (2.11–30) with its conclusion 'you ought not to grieve' (na śocitum arhasi, repeated at 2.25, 2.26, 2.27, 2.30).

original.text:
svadharmamapi cāvekṣya na vikampitumarhasi|
dharmyāddhi yuddhāchreyo'nyatkṣatriyasya na vidyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: and considering your own dharma (svadharma) too, you ought not to waver; for a kṣatriya there is nothing better than a battle that accords with dharma (dharmya).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Opens the second argument (2.31–37): from one's own dharma and honour, after the argument from the nature of the self (2.11–30).

original.text:
yadṛcchayā copapannaṃ svargadvāramapāvṛtam|
sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddhamīdṛśam

translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

atha caittvamimaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ na kariṣyasi|

original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: making pleasure and pain the same, gain and loss, victory and defeat, then engage (yujyasva) in battle; thus you will not incur sin (pāpa).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Turning point: fighting with equanimity is said not to incur sin — the first statement of the teaching that the manner of acting, not the act alone, decides its binding result.

original.text:
eṣā te'bhihitā sāṃkhye buddhiryoge tvimāṃ śrṛṇu|
buddhyāyukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṃ prahāsyasi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: this understanding (buddhi) has been declared to you in [the way of] sāṃkhya; now hear it in [the way of] yoga — yoked with which understanding, Pārtha, you will cast off the bondage of action (karma-bandha).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

Edition encoding artefact: 'śrṛṇu' stands for śṛṇu; the original text is kept exactly as in the segment.

svalpamapyasya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Praise and stated result of the yoga: even a little of it is not wasted. 'pratyavāya' is the ritual term for the harm of a defective or omitted rite.

original.text:
vyavasāyātmikā buddhirekeha kurunandana|
bahuśākhā hyanantāśca buddhayo'vyavasāyinām

speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

yāmimāṃ puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ pravadantyavipaścitaḥ|
vedavādaratāḥ pārtha nānyadastīti vādinaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: the flowery speech that the undiscerning (avipaścit) proclaim, Pārtha — those who delight in the statements of the Veda (veda-vāda-rata) and say 'there is nothing else' —
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
kāmātmānaḥ svargaparā janmakarmaphalapradām|
kriyāviśeṣabahulāṃ bhogaiśvaryagatiṃ prati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: — whose selves are made of desire (kāmātman), intent on heaven (svarga-para) — [speech] that offers birth as the fruit of action (janma-karma-phala-prada), abounding in particular rites (kriyā-viśeṣa) aimed at enjoyment and lordship (bhoga-aiśvarya) —
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

bhogaiśvaryaprasaktānāṃ tayāpahṛtacetasām|
vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: — for those attached to enjoyment and lordship, whose minds (cetas) are carried away by that [speech], the understanding whose nature is resolve is not established in samādhi.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'samādhau na vidhīyate': commentators gloss samādhi here as the mind/inner organ or as concentrated absorption; the minimal sense is that resolute understanding does not become settled in such people.

original.text:
traiguṇyaviṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna|
nirdvandvo nityasattvastho niryogakṣema ātmavān
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yāvānartha udapāne sarvataḥ saṃplutodake|
tāvānsarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: as much use as there is in a well (udapāna) when there is flooding water on every side, so much is there in all the Vedas for a brāhmaṇa who knows (vijānataḥ).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:

original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

siddhyasiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: established in yoga (yogastha), perform actions, Dhanañjaya, abandoning attachment (saṅga), being the same in success and failure; sameness (samatva) is called yoga.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:

original.text:
śrutivipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā|
samādhāvacalā buddhistadā yogamavāpsyasi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: when your understanding, perplexed by what it has heard (śruti-vipratipannā), stands unmoving, immovable in samādhi, then you will attain yoga.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:
sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhisthasya keśava|
sthitadhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta kimāsīta vrajeta kim
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Arjuna: what is the description (bhāṣā) of one whose wisdom is steady (sthita-prajña), who is established in samādhi (samādhi-stha), Keśava? How does one of steady thought (sthita-dhī) speak, how does he sit, how does he move?
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Opens the section on the person of steady wisdom (2.54–72). Arjuna asks for marks (bhāṣā) and for how such a person speaks, sits and moves; the answer describes inner marks more than outward behaviour.

original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha manogatān|
ātmanyevātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthitaprajñastadocyate

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:
duḥkheṣvanudvignamanāḥ sukheṣu vigataspṛhaḥ|
vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ sthitadhīrmunirucyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: one whose mind is not shaken in sorrows, who has no craving (spṛhā) in pleasures, from whom passion (rāga), fear and anger (krodha) have gone — he is called a sage (muni) of steady thought.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:
yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehastattatprāpya śubhāśubham|
nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: he who is without attachment (anabhisneha) everywhere, who, meeting this or that, pleasant or unpleasant (śubhāśubha), neither rejoices nor hates — his wisdom is firmly established (prajñā pratiṣṭhitā).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yadā saṃharate cāyaṃ kūrmo'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ|
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: and when, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs on all sides, he withdraws the senses (indriya) from the objects of the senses (indriyārtha), his wisdom is firmly established.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The tortoise simile for withdrawing the senses from their objects.

original.text:
viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ|
rasavarjaṃ raso'pyasya paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: sense-objects (viṣaya) turn away from the embodied one who does not feed on them (nirāhāra), except the taste (rasa) for them; even the taste turns away from him when he has seen the highest (param dṛṣṭvā).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'nirāhāra' (not taking in) is read as abstaining from sense-objects generally or, more narrowly, as fasting; the verse states that such abstention leaves the inner taste (rasa) behind, and that only seeing 'the highest' (param; commentators: the self/Brahman/the Lord) removes it. The verse does not prescribe fasting.

original.text:
yatato hyapi kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ|
indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṃ manaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: for the turbulent (pramāthin) senses, son of Kuntī, forcibly carry off the mind (manas) even of a discerning person (vipaścit) who is striving.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: A warning: effort and discernment alone do not keep the mind from being carried off by the senses.

original.text:
tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya yukta āsīta matparaḥ|
vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: restraining them all, let him sit yoked (yukta āsīta), intent on me (mat-para); for he whose senses are under control — his wisdom is firmly established.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: First place in the text where Kṛṣṇa names himself as the one to be intent on (mat-para) while restraining the senses; commentators differ on how much devotional weight to give it here.

original.text:
dhyāyato viṣayānpuṃsaḥ saṅgasteṣūpajāyate|
saṅgāt saṃjāyate kāmaḥ kāmātkrodho'bhijāyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
krodhādbhavati saṃmohaḥ saṃmohātsmṛtivibhramaḥ|
smṛtibhraṃśād buddhināśo buddhināśātpraṇaśyati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: from anger comes delusion (saṃmoha); from delusion, confusion of memory (smṛti-vibhrama); from the loss of memory, the destruction of understanding (buddhi-nāśa); from the destruction of understanding, one perishes.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
rāgadveṣaviyuktaistu viṣayānindriyaiścaran|
ātmavaśyairvidheyātmā prasādamadhigacchati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: but one who moves among sense-objects with senses free from passion and aversion (rāga-dveṣa) and under the self's control, being self-governed (vidheyātman), attains serenity (prasāda).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The remedy is stated as moving among objects with mastered senses, not as avoiding them.

original.text:
prasāde sarvaduḥkhānāṃ hānirasyopajāyate|
prasannacetaso hyāśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: in serenity (prasāda) there arises for him the ending of all sorrows; for the understanding of one whose mind is serene (prasanna-cetas) quickly becomes steady.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
nāsti buddhirayuktasya na cāyuktasya bhāvanā|
na cābhāvayataḥ śāntiraśāntasya kutaḥ sukham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: for one who is not yoked (ayukta) there is no understanding (buddhi), nor is there contemplation (bhāvanā) for the unyoked; for one without contemplation there is no peace (śānti), and for one without peace, where is happiness?
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'bhāvanā' is glossed variously (steady contemplation, dwelling on the self, conviction); the verse gives it as the link between being yoked and peace.

original.text:
indriyāṇāṃ hi caratāṃ yanmano'nuvidhīyate|
tadasya harati prajñāṃ vāyurnāvamivāmbhasi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: for when the mind (manas) is led along by the roving senses, it carries off his wisdom (prajñā), as the wind carries off a ship on the water.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The subject of 'carries off' (tad) is the mind that follows the senses (or the one sense the mind follows); the simile is the wind and the ship.

original.text:
tasmādyasya mahābāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ|
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: therefore, mighty-armed one, he whose senses are withheld on all sides from the objects of the senses — his wisdom is firmly established.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī|
yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: what is night for all beings, in that the self-restrained one (saṃyamin) is awake; that in which beings are awake is night for the sage (muni) who sees.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: A reversal image; the verse does not say what the 'night' and the 'waking' are. Commentators take the night of beings as the highest reality (to which they are asleep) and their waking as the world of objects and distinctions.

original.text:
āpūryamāṇamacalapratiṣṭhaṃ
samudramāpaḥ praviśanti yadvat|
tadvatkāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve
sa śāntimāpnoti na kāmakāmī
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: as the waters enter the ocean, which is ever being filled yet stays unmoved in its foundation, so he whom all desires (kāma) enter attains peace (śānti) — not the one who desires desires (kāma-kāmin).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
vihāya kāmānyaḥ sarvānpumāṃścarati niḥspṛhaḥ|
nirmamo nirahaṃkāraḥ sa śāṃtimadhigacchati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: the person who, abandoning all desires, moves about free from craving (niḥspṛha), without 'mine' (nirmama), without the sense of 'I' (nirahaṃkāra) — he attains peace.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati|
sthitvā'syāmantakāle'pi brahmanirvāṇamṛcchati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: this is the brahmic state (brāhmī sthiti), Pārtha; having attained it one is not bewildered. Abiding in it even at the time of death (anta-kāla), one attains the nirvāṇa of Brahman (brahma-nirvāṇa).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Closing verse of chapter 2 and first use of 'brahmanirvāṇa' in the text (again at 5.24–26). 'Even at the time of death' (antakāle 'pi) links the state to the last moment (cf. 8.5).

paraphrase: Chapter 2 opens the teaching. 2.1–10 (frame): Kṛṣṇa rebukes Arjuna's faintness and unmanliness (2.2–3); Arjuna restates his dilemma — he cannot fight Bhīṣma and Droṇa, would rather live on alms, does not know which outcome is better — and asks Kṛṣṇa, as his disciple who has come for refuge, to tell him for certain what is better (śreyas) (2.4–8); he says 'I will not fight' and falls silent, and Kṛṣṇa, as if smiling, answers (2.9–10). 2.11–30: the teaching on the embodied self (dehin): the wise do not grieve; the self was never not and will never cease; it passes through bodies as through the ages of life and as through garments; the unreal has no being and the real no non-being; the self neither slays nor is slain, is unborn, eternal, uncuttable, unmanifest and unthinkable; even on the contrary view birth and death are inevitable; therefore do not grieve. 2.31–38: the argument from one's own dharma (svadharma) and honour: a dharmic battle is the kṣatriya's best good and a door to heaven, refusal brings sin and disgrace; fight treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike. 2.39: transition — the understanding (buddhi) given 'in sāṃkhya' is now given 'in yoga'. 2.40–53: the yoga of understanding (buddhi-yoga): resolute understanding is one (2.41); the flowery speech of those who delight in Vedic statements and seek heaven and power keeps understanding from samādhi; the Vedas concern the three guṇas, be free of them (2.42–46); your right is to action, not its fruits; yoga is sameness and skill in actions; the wise, yoked with understanding, abandon the fruit and are freed from the bondage of birth (2.47–51); when understanding passes beyond delusion and stands steady in samādhi, you will attain yoga (2.52–53). 2.54–72: Arjuna asks about the person of steady wisdom (sthitaprajña); Kṛṣṇa describes him: he gives up all desires and is content in the self, unshaken by sorrow and pleasure, free from passion, fear and anger, withdraws the senses like a tortoise (2.55–61); the chain from dwelling on objects through attachment, desire, anger, delusion and loss of memory to ruin (2.62–63), and its reverse through mastered senses to serenity and steady understanding (2.64–68); the sage is awake where beings sleep, is filled by desires like the ocean yet unmoved, and without 'mine' and 'I' attains peace (2.69–71); this is the brahmic state, reaching which even at death one attains brahma-nirvāṇa (2.72). The chapter's purpose, as it presents itself, is to answer Arjuna's grief and his request for the good, first by knowledge of the self, then by the discipline of action done with steady understanding, culminating in the portrait of the one whose wisdom is steady.
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Printed editions carry a colophon naming the chapter (commonly 'Sāṃkhyayoga'); the colophon is not among this edition's segments.

original.text:
jyāyasī cetkarmaṇaste matā buddhirjanārdana|
tatkiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Arjuna: if understanding (buddhi) is held by you to be superior to action (karma), Janārdana, then why do you urge me into this terrible action, Keśava?
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Arjuna's question takes up 2.49 (action far inferior to buddhi-yoga). It opens chapter 3 and states one side of the question of understanding versus action.

original.text:
vyāmiśreṇeva vākyena buddhiṃ mohayasīva me|
tadekaṃ vada niśicatya yena śreyo'hamāpnuyām
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Arjuna: with speech that seems mixed (vyāmiśra) you seem to confuse my understanding; tell me decisively the one thing by which I may attain the good (śreyas).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'iva' (seems) is used twice: Arjuna says the speech only seems mixed and only seems to confuse him. Edition encoding artefact: 'niśicatya' stands for niścitya (decisively); the original text is kept exactly as in the segment.

original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
loke'smindvividhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayānagha|
jñānayogena sāṃkhyānāṃ karmayogena yoginām
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: in this world a twofold commitment (niṣṭhā) was declared by me of old, sinless one: through the yoga of knowledge (jñāna-yoga) for the sāṃkhyas, and through the yoga of action (karma-yoga) for the yogins.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Kṛṣṇa presents himself as the original declarer of both commitments ('purā proktā mayā'); cf. the ancient transmission of 'this yoga' at 4.1–3. Commentators divide on whether the two niṣṭhās are for two different kinds of person, or are successive stages for one person.

original.text:
na karmaṇāmanārambhānnaiṣkarmyaṃ puruṣo'śnute|
na ca saṃnyasanādeva siddhiṃ samadhigacchati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: a person does not attain freedom from action (naiṣkarmya) by not undertaking actions, nor does one reach perfection (siddhi) by renunciation (saṃnyasana) alone.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'eva' (alone/merely) qualifies renunciation: the verse denies that mere renunciation brings perfection, not that renunciation has no place; commentators read the relation of action, purification and renunciation differently.

original.text:
na hi kaśicatkṣaṇamapi jātu tiṣṭhatyakarmakṛt|
kāryate hyavaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛtijairguṇaiḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: for no one ever remains even for a moment without doing action; everyone is made to act, helplessly, by the guṇas born of prakṛti.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
karmendriyāṇi saṃyamya ya āste manasā smaran|
indriyārthānvimūḍhātmā mithyācāraḥ sa ucyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:
yastvindriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate'rjuna|
karmendriyaiḥ karmayogamasaktaḥ sa viśiṣyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: but he who, controlling the senses by the mind, Arjuna, undertakes the yoga of action (karma-yoga) with the organs of action, without attachment (asakta) — he excels.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
niyataṃ kuru karma tvaṃ karma jyāyo hyakarmaṇaḥ|
śarīrayātrāpi ca te na prasiddhyedakarmaṇaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: perform your allotted action (niyataṃ karma), for action is better than inaction (akarman); even the maintenance of your body (śarīra-yātrā) could not be accomplished through inaction.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:
yajñārthātkarmaṇo'nyatra loko'yaṃ karmabandhanaḥ|
tadarthaṃ karma kaunteya muktasaṃgaḥ samācara
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: this world is bound by action (karma-bandhana) except for action done for the sake of sacrifice (yajñārtha); for that purpose, son of Kuntī, free from attachment (mukta-saṅga), perform action.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Some commentators gloss 'yajña' here as Viṣṇu (citing the Vedic statement 'yajño vai viṣṇuḥ'); the verse itself says only 'for the sake of sacrifice'. 3.10–16 go on to speak of sacrifice in the ritual and cosmic sense.

original.text:
sahayajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovāca prajāpatiḥ|
anena prasaviṣyadhvameṣa vo'stviṣṭakāmadhuk
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: in the beginning Prajāpati, having created beings together with sacrifice (saha-yajñāḥ), said: 'By this you shall bring forth offspring (prasaviṣyadhvam); let this be for you the cow that yields what you desire (iṣṭa-kāma-dhuk).'
speaker: Kṛṣṇa (quoting Prajāpati)
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
devānbhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ|
parasparaṃ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ paramavāpsyatha
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Prajāpati's words (quoted by Kṛṣṇa): 'With this nourish (bhāvayata) the gods, and let the gods nourish you; nourishing one another, you will attain the highest good (śreyaḥ param).'
speaker: Kṛṣṇa (quoting Prajāpati)
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The addressees are the beings created with sacrifice (plural 'you').

original.text:
iṣṭānbhogānhi vo devā dāsyante yajñabhāvitāḥ|
tairdattānapradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: 'For the gods, nourished by sacrifice, will give you the enjoyments you desire.' He who enjoys what they have given without offering to them is simply a thief (stena).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa (quoting Prajāpati, at least in the first half)
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The text does not mark where Prajāpati's quoted words end; the first half continues his address ('vo', to you), the second half is a general statement.

original.text:
yajñaśiṣṭāśinaḥ santo mucyante sarvakilbiṣaiḥ|
bhuñjate te tvaghaṃ pāpā ye pacantyātmakāraṇāt
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: the good (santaḥ) who eat the remains of sacrifice (yajña-śiṣṭa) are released from all faults (kilbiṣa); but the wicked who cook only for their own sake eat sin (agha).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
annādbhavanti bhūtāni parjanyādannasambhavaḥ|
yajñādbhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karmasamudbhavaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: beings come from food (anna); food is produced from rain (parjanya); rain comes from sacrifice (yajña); sacrifice arises from action (karma).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Compare the ritual-cosmic cycle in Manusmṛti 3.76 (offering → sun → rain → food → creatures) and 'from food beings are born' in Taittirīya Upaniṣad 3.2 (thematic parallels; refs from memory).

original.text:
karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmākṣarasamudbhavam|
tasmātsarvagataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: know action (karma) to arise from brahman, and brahman to arise from the imperishable (akṣara); therefore the all-pervading (sarvagata) brahman is ever established in sacrifice.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Difficult verse. Commentators divide on 'brahma' here: the Veda (so that action is prescribed by the Veda, which issues from the Imperishable), or prakṛti/the body (from which action arises); and on 'sarvagataṃ brahma' accordingly. The paraphrase keeps the Sanskrit words.

original.text:
evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ|
aghāyurindriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: he who does not keep turning here the wheel (cakra) thus set in motion, whose life is sin (aghāyu) and who delights in the senses (indriyārāma) — he lives in vain, Pārtha.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Closes the account of the wheel of sacrifice (3.10–16).

original.text:
yastvātmaratireva syādātmatṛptaśca mānavaḥ|
ātmanyeva ca santuṣṭastasya kāryaṃ na vidyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: but the person who delights in the self alone (ātma-rati), is satisfied in the self (ātma-tṛpta), and is content in the self alone — for him there is nothing that has to be done (kāryaṃ na vidyate).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Commentators divide on whether 3.17–18 exempt the knower of the self from all action (so that 3.19 addresses Arjuna as not yet such), or describe the inner freedom of one who nonetheless goes on acting.

original.text:
naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaścana|
na cāsya sarvabhūteṣu kaśicadarthavyapāśrayaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: for him there is no purpose (artha) at all in what is done here, nor in what is not done; nor does he depend on any being for any purpose.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Edition encoding artefact: 'kaśicad' stands for kaścid; the original text is kept exactly as in the segment.

original.text:
tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara|
asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti pūruṣaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: therefore, always unattached (asakta), perform the action that is to be done (kāryaṃ karma); for by performing action unattached, a person attains the highest (param).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'tasmāt' (therefore) is referred by commentators either to the preceding verses on the self-content person or back to the argument of 3.8–16.

original.text:
karmaṇaiva hi saṃsiddhimāsthitā janakādayaḥ|
lokasaṃgrahamevāpi saṃpaśyankartumarhasi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: for it was by action alone (karmaṇaiva) that Janaka and others attained perfection (saṃsiddhi); and looking also to the holding together of the world (loka-saṃgraha), you ought to act.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Janaka is cited as precedent. Commentators divide on whether 'saṃsiddhi' here means liberation reached through action, or the purification that leads to it.

original.text:
yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ|
sa yatpramāṇaṃ kurute lokastadanuvartate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: whatever the best person (śreṣṭha) does, that alone other people do; whatever standard (pramāṇa) he sets, the world follows.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
na me pārthāsti kartavyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiñcana|
nānavāptamavāptavyaṃ varta eva ca karmaṇi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: for me, Pārtha, there is nothing whatever to be done in the three worlds, nothing unattained to be attained; yet I continue in action.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yadi hyahaṃ na varteyaṃ jātu karmaṇyatandritaḥ|
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: for if I did not ever continue unwearied in action, people everywhere would follow my path (vartman), Pārtha.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
utsīdeyurime lokā na kuryāṃ karma cedaham|
saṅkarasya ca kartā syāmupahanyāmimāḥ prajāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: these worlds would perish if I did not perform action; I would be the maker of confusion (saṅkara) and would destroy these beings (prajā).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'saṅkara' is read as the mixture of social orders (as in 1.41–43) or more generally as confusion/disorder.

original.text:
saktāḥ karmaṇyavidvāṃso yathā kurvanti bhārata|
kuryādvidvāṃstathāsaktaśicakīrṣurlokasaṃgraham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: as the unwise (avidvāṃsaḥ), attached to action, act, Bhārata, so should the wise (vidvān) act, unattached, wishing to hold the world together (loka-saṃgraha).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

tags.stage_native: vidvān (the wise) contrasted with avidvān (the unwise, attached to action)

translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Edition encoding artefact: 'saktaśicakīrṣur' stands for saktaś cikīrṣur; the original text is kept exactly as in the segment.

original.text:
na buddhibhedaṃ janayedajñānāṃ karmasaṅginām|
joṣayetsarvakarmāṇi vidvān yuktaḥ samācaran
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: let the wise one not cause a split in the understanding (buddhi-bheda) of the ignorant who are attached to action; acting himself while yoked (yukta), he should make them take delight in all actions.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

tags.stage_native: vidvān (the wise) guiding ajña karma-saṅgin (the ignorant attached to action)

translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: An explicit distinction of adhikāra: the wise are told not to unsettle the ignorant who are attached to action. 'joṣayet' (make them delight in / engage in) is read as encouraging them to act.

original.text:
prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ|
ahaṅkāravimūḍhātmā kartā'hamiti manyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: actions are in every case being done by the guṇas of prakṛti; one whose self is deluded by the sense of 'I' (ahaṃkāra-vimūḍhātman) thinks 'I am the doer' (kartā aham).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Tagged 'bridging' because the verse sets what actually acts (the guṇas) against how the deluded take it ('I am the doer').

original.text:
tattvavittu mahābāho guṇakarmavibhāgayoḥ|
guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: but one who knows the truth (tattvavid), mighty-armed one, about the division of the guṇas and their actions (guṇa-karma-vibhāga), thinking 'the guṇas move among the guṇas', is not attached.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'guṇā guṇeṣu vartante' is taken by commentators as the guṇas in the form of the senses moving among the guṇas in the form of objects; cf. 14.23 ('guṇā vartanta ity eva').

original.text:
prakṛterguṇasammūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇakarmasu|
tānakṛtsnavido mandānkṛtsnavinna vicālayet
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: those deluded by the guṇas of prakṛti are attached to the actions of the guṇas; one who knows the whole (kṛtsna-vid) should not unsettle those dull ones (manda) who do not know the whole.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

tags.stage_native: kṛtsnavid (knower of the whole) and akṛtsnavid / manda (the dull who know in part)

translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Repeats the adhikāra rule of 3.26.

original.text:
mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasyādhyātmacetasā|
nirāśīrnirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigatajvaraḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: resigning all actions to me (mayi saṃnyasya), with your mind on the self (adhyātma-cetas), free from expectation (nirāśīḥ) and from 'mine' (nirmama), fight, your fever gone (vigata-jvara).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'adhyātmacetasā' is glossed variously (with a mind directed to the self; with the discerning thought that one acts for the Lord). Compare 18.57 (cetasā sarvakarmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya).

original.text:
ye me matamidaṃ nityamanutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ|
śraddhāvanto'nasūyanto mucyante te'pi karmabhiḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: those people who constantly follow this teaching (mata) of mine, having faith (śraddhā) and not cavilling (anasūyantaḥ), they too are released from actions (karmabhiḥ).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Stated result (phala) for those who follow the teaching with faith.

original.text:
ye tvetadabhyasūyanto nānutiṣṭhanti me matam|
sarvajñānavimūḍhāṃstānviddhi naṣṭānacetasaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: but those who, cavilling (abhyasūyantaḥ), do not follow this teaching of mine — know them, deluded in all knowledge (sarva-jñāna-vimūḍha) and senseless, to be lost.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
sadṛśaṃ ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛterjñānavānapi|
prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: even a person of knowledge (jñānavān) acts in accordance with his own nature (prakṛti); beings follow their nature — what will restraint (nigraha) accomplish?
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Commentators reconcile this verse with the call to restraint in 3.34 and 3.41 in different ways (e.g. that forced suppression against one's nature is futile, while not coming under the sway of attraction and aversion is possible). The verse by itself states the power of one's nature.

original.text:
indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāgadveṣau vyavasthitau|
tayorna vaśamāgacchettau hyasya paripanthinau
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: attraction and aversion (rāga-dveṣa) are set in the object of each sense; one should not come under their sway, for they are his waylayers (paripanthin).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt|
svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: better is one's own dharma (svadharma), though lacking in merit (viguṇa), than another's dharma (paradharma) well performed; death in one's own dharma is better; another's dharma brings danger (bhayāvaha).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The first line recurs at 18.47.

original.text:
atha kena prayukto'yaṃ pāpaṃ carati pūruṣaḥ|
anicchannapi vārṣṇeya balādiva niyojitaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Arjuna: then, impelled by what, Vārṣṇeya, does a person commit sin (pāpa), even against his will, as if forced by violence?
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Arjuna's question opens the last section of chapter 3 (3.36–43).

original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajoguṇasamudbhavaḥ|
mahāśano mahāpāpmā viddhyenamiha vairiṇam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: it is desire (kāma), it is anger (krodha), arising from the guṇa of rajas (rajo-guṇa-samudbhava), all-devouring (mahāśana), greatly sinful (mahā-pāpman); know this to be the enemy (vairin) here.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Desire and anger are named with a single pronoun ('eṣa', this one) as one enemy; commentators take anger as desire obstructed. Cf. 16.21 (desire, anger and greed as the threefold gate of hell).

original.text:
dhūmenāvriyate vahniryathā''darśo malena ca|
yatholbenāvṛto garbhastathā tenedamāvṛtam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: as fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and an embryo by the womb-membrane (ulba), so this is covered by it (desire).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'idam' (this) is taken as knowledge (so 3.39) or as this world/the embodied; the three similes are read by commentators as grades of covering.

original.text:
āvṛtaṃ jñānametena jñānino nityavairiṇā|
kāmarūpeṇa kaunteya duṣpūreṇānalena ca
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: knowledge (jñāna) is covered by this constant enemy of the knower (jñānin), son of Kuntī — by desire in form (kāma-rūpa), an insatiable (duṣpūra) fire.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
indriyāṇi mano buddhirasyādhiṣṭhānamucyate|
etairvimohayatyeṣa jñānamāvṛtya dehinam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: the senses (indriya), mind (manas) and understanding (buddhi) are said to be its seat (adhiṣṭhāna); through these it deludes the embodied one (dehin), covering knowledge.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
tasmāttvamindriyāṇyādau niyamya bharatarṣabha|
pāpmānaṃ prajahi hyenaṃ jñānavijñānanāśanam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: therefore, bull of the Bharatas, first restraining the senses, slay this evil one (pāpman), the destroyer of knowledge and discernment (jñāna-vijñāna).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'jñāna-vijñāna' is glossed as knowledge (from teaching) and its realisation/particular knowledge; commentators differ.

original.text:
indriyāṇi parāṇyāhurindriyebhyaḥ paraṃ manaḥ|
manasastu parā buddhiryo buddheḥ paratastu saḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: the senses, they say, are high (para); higher than the senses is the mind (manas); higher than the mind is the understanding (buddhi); but what is higher than the understanding is he (saḥ).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

notes: Closing verse of chapter 3. 4.1 continues directly with 'this yoga' (imaṃ yogam) taught to Vivasvat.

paraphrase: Chapter 3 answers the question of understanding versus action. 3.1–2: Arjuna asks why, if understanding (buddhi) is held superior to action, Kṛṣṇa urges him to terrible action, and asks for one decisive teaching. 3.3–9: Kṛṣṇa says he declared of old a twofold commitment (niṣṭhā) — the yoga of knowledge for the sāṃkhyas and the yoga of action for the yogins; actionlessness (naiṣkarmya) is not reached by not acting nor perfection by mere renunciation; no one can stay without acting, since the guṇas of prakṛti make everyone act; restraining the organs of action while the mind dwells on objects is hypocrisy, while karma-yoga with the senses controlled and without attachment excels; do your allotted action, for the world is bound by action except action for sacrifice. 3.10–16: Prajāpati created beings with sacrifice, telling them to nourish the gods and be nourished; who enjoys the gods' gifts without offering is a thief; eating the remains of sacrifice frees from fault; the wheel of food, rain, sacrifice, action, brahman and the imperishable must be kept turning. 3.17–18: for one who delights and is content in the self there is nothing that must be done. 3.19–26: therefore act unattached; Janaka and others reached perfection by action; act for the holding together of the world (loka-saṃgraha), since people follow the best; Kṛṣṇa himself, needing nothing, keeps acting lest the worlds perish; the wise should act unattached as the unwise act attached, and not unsettle the understanding of the ignorant. 3.27–29: actions are done by the guṇas, and only the ego-deluded thinks 'I am the doer'; the knower of the truth is not attached. 3.30–32: resign all actions to Kṛṣṇa and fight; those who follow this teaching with faith are released, those who cavil are lost. 3.33–35: all beings follow their nature; attraction and aversion lie in wait in the sense-objects; one's own dharma, though imperfect, is better than another's. 3.36–43: Arjuna asks what drives a person to sin against his will; Kṛṣṇa names desire and anger, born of rajas, the enemy that covers knowledge as smoke covers fire, seated in the senses, mind and understanding; restrain the senses first, know what is beyond understanding, steady the self by the self and slay desire. The chapter's purpose, as it presents itself, is to show why Arjuna must act — action being unavoidable, sacrificial, exemplary and non-binding when done without attachment — and to name desire as what must be overcome.
